title: Intelligent Textbooks
extended_summary:
This editorial surveys the evolution of the intelligent textbooks research area and positions recent work within a five-generation framework: engineered intelligence, integrated intelligence, extracted intelligence, datamined intelligence, and generated intelligence. The paper asks how digital textbooks can be made more adaptive, interactive, and supportive for learners by combining classical AI, knowledge graphs, NLP/ML, learning analytics, and recent generative AI methods.

The article does not report a single empirical intervention with participants. Instead, it reviews representative systems and workshop contributions, including adaptive interfaces, smart content, knowledge extraction from textbooks, interaction mining from learner logs, and LLM-based tools for question answering, explanations, and feedback. It also highlights domain-specific applications such as programming, medicine, and K-12 textbook visions, along with phygital textbook companions that connect paper and digital formats.

The main conclusion is that intelligent textbooks are increasingly powered by large-scale extraction of textbook content and learner interaction data, with generative AI opening new possibilities for explanations, questions, and conversational support. The authors argue that the field has matured but still needs careful calibration with real teacher-learner interaction, stronger pedagogical grounding, and better understanding of how to use these technologies effectively in practice.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an editorial and field overview, not an empirical evaluation of Khanmigo or any other intervention. It cites prior work and examples, but does not present a primary study design, sample, or measured outcomes for the target intervention.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct learning or implementation effects are measured in this paper, so there is no evidentiary basis for estimating impact size. The paper is useful for conceptual framing, but it does not demonstrate outcome impact for K-12 science instruction.

interventions.use_case: Editorial/review discussion of Khan Academy's Khanmigo as a GPT-4-based tutoring chatbot around educational content, described as a generative-AI learner support tool for interactive textbook-style tutoring and question answering.
